item.title: Fire breaks out at Madani Super Market, 4 units battling blaze
item.description:
A fire broke out at Madani Super Market in Hemayetpur, Savar, on Wednesday evening.
The blaze erupted at the market near Hemayetpur bus stand in Tetuljhora Union around 6:00pm, prompting four Fire Service and Civil Defence units to rush to the scene.
Two units from Tannery Fire Station and two from Savar Fire Station are working to bring the fire under control.
No casualties were reported immediately. Firefighter Md Tushar Ali of Tannery Fire Service confirmed the incident, saying the cause of the fire was not immediately known.
He said the cause of the fire and extent of damage would be determined after the blaze is brought under control.

item.title: Attempt to erase Tagore portrait: Lawyers clash during bail hearing of 2 accused
item.description:
A scuffle broke out between lawyers during a bail hearing at a Dhaka court on Wednesday in a case over an attempt to erase a portrait of Rabindranath Tagore painted on a wall outside Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy, prompting the judge to leave the courtroom temporarily before returning to reject the bail petitions of two accused.
Several lawyers on the prosecution side allegedly assaulted a defense lawyer after he objected to remarks made by the public prosecutor, leading to shouting and disorder inside the courtroom.
The accused, Al Nur Mohammad Ayas, also known as A N M Ayas, and Marzia Khandaker Rimi, were brought before Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Riyad Hasan. Their lawyer, Monir Hossain Sumon, sought bail for both.
Sumon argued that the case concerned the application of ink to Tagore's portrait and that the charges brought against his clients did not apply. He said that while some people loved Tagore, others disliked him, adding that the poet was neither a divine being nor an angel.
He also told the court that Ayas was ill and requested bail for both accused.
Dhaka Metropolitan Public Prosecutor Omar Faruque Faruqi opposed the petitions, alleging that Ayas had made statements about Pakistan and visiting the tomb of Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
Faruqi alleged that the remarks contained provocation and ulterior motives, and that the accused were attempting to create division by bringing Pakistan and India into the discussion.
He also questioned why the graffiti had been painted after hawkers were removed from Segunbagicha. He said people could advocate displaying portraits of Ghulam Azam and Matiur Rahman Nizami, but could not deface another person's portrait.
Faruqi further alleged that the accused had acted to provoke the Hindu community. He also accused them of abusing the government and the public over the past 7 months and teaching younger people to use abusive language.
Addressing the lawyers representing Ayas and Rimi, Faruqi said it was clear that they were all Jamaat-e-Islami lawyers.
Defense lawyer Al Mohsin Touhid objected to the public prosecutor's remarks. Several lawyers on the prosecution side then allegedly attacked him with punches and blows, tearing his shirt.
Some lawyers said Touhid was unwell, while others intervened and pulled him away from the confrontation.
As the shouting and disorder continued, the judge left the courtroom. A few minutes later, Faruqi and defense lawyer Monir Hossain Sumon brought the situation under control.
While standing in the dock, Ayas appealed to Faruqi, saying: “I have apologised, sir. I apologise. Please, I am sorry.”
Addressing the lawyers, he asked: “Will you destroy my life by doing this?”
Speaking to Touhid, Ayas said: “I do not know you. Why did you come?”
Another lawyer then rebuked Ayas, saying that Touhid did not know him.
Riyad Hasan later returned to the courtroom and expressed his displeasure over the incident.
“I felt very bad about what happened. I did not expect this from you. I am issuing the order at this stage,” he said.
The judge subsequently rejected the bail petitions and ordered that both accused be sent to jail.
While being taken from the court to jail under tight security, Ayas said: “Have I committed murder? Why are you taking me like this?”
He was later taken to the detention facility of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) Court.
On Saturday, October 10, Ayas and a group of young people faced police obstruction while attempting to erase a portrait of Rabindranath Tagore painted on a wall in front of Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy in Dhaka.
Following an exchange of words between the group and police, officers detained 4 people, including Ayas, and took them to the police station.
A woman was seen applying ink to the portrait before a police officer intervened. The woman said they had come to protest against “Indian aggression.” Despite police intervention, members of the State Dialogue Forum, led by its member secretary A N M Ayas, continued chanting slogans.
Shahbagh police station Sub-Inspector Ziaul Haque filed a case on Saturday over the attempt to erase Tagore's portrait.
The accused were charged with criminal conspiracy, creating enmity between different groups and hurting religious sentiments.
On Sunday, the court granted 2 days of remand for Marzia Khandaker Rimi and Sujon, and 3 days for Ayas and Sakibul Hasan.
On Tuesday, Sakibul Hasan and Sujon Mia were sent to jail after completing their remand.
On Wednesday, Ayas and Rimi were produced before the court after completing their remand. Shahbagh police station Sub-Inspector Abdul Gaffar Himel, the investigation officer in the case, applied for an order to keep them in jail.
The application stated that investigators had obtained important information during remand about other absconding suspects allegedly involved in the incident. The information was being verified, it said.
It further stated that keeping the 2 accused in jail was necessary until the investigation was completed and their names and addresses were verified. It also said they might need to be taken into police remand again for further and more detailed questioning in the interest of the investigation.

item.title: Mirza Abbas returns to Dhaka after treatment in Malaysia
item.description:
BNP Standing Committee member and Political Adviser to the Prime Minister Mirza Abbas returned home on Wednesday night after receiving medical treatment in Malaysia.
Abbas arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport aboard a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight around 9pm, accompanied by his wife Afroza Abbas and son Mirza Yasir Abbas, his Assistant Private Secretary (APS) Mizanur Rahman Sohel said.
"Sir has returned home after completing his treatment and is doing much better now," his APS added.
Mirza Abbas had travelled to Malaysia on September 16 for follow-up treatment at Prince Court Medical Centre.
Earlier, on March 11, the veteran politician fell ill during Iftar, lost consciousness, and was rushed to Evercare Hospital in Dhaka, where doctors diagnosed him with a brain haemorrhage. Following emergency surgery, he was flown to Singapore via air ambulance and underwent treatment at Singapore General Hospital for one and a half months before being transferred to Prince Court Medical Centre in Malaysia.
After nearly five months of medical care in Singapore and Malaysia, Abbas initially returned to Bangladesh on September 2 before departing again for follow-up care.

item.title: Three held over online job scam
item.description:
Three alleged online fraudsters have been arrested in Khulna’s Batiaghata upazila for swindling an expatriate out of Tk88,890 by promising him an online job.
The 3rd Armed Police Battalion (APBn) arrested Sabbir Hossain, Swadhon Kumar Ghatak and Shakib Sheikh on Tuesday following a cybercrime investigation. The suspects were later handed over to Bandar police in Narayanganj, where a case was filed on October 12.
Additional DIG MM Salahuddin, commander of the 3rd APBn in Khulna, said the suspects allegedly used social media to lure people with promises of online work and defraud them of money.
Police seized five mobile phones, 15 SIM cards and Tk500 in cash from their possession.

item.title: Hasanul Haq Inu taken back to jail after medical check-up
item.description:
Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JSD) President and former information minister Hasanul Haq Inu was taken back to jail after undergoing a medical check-up at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) on Wednesday evening.
He was taken to the hospital’s emergency department under the supervision of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), with assistance from the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP).
CID Inspector Nasir Uddin Sarker said Inu underwent an initial medical examination at the emergency department before officials took him away at around 6:30pm.
Inu was arrested by police in Dhaka’s Uttara area on August 26, 2024, following the fall of the Awami League government. He is facing trial in multiple cases before the International Crimes Tribunal.

item.title: 107 DNCC residents receive livelihood support equipment
item.description:
More than 100 residents of low-income communities in Dhaka North have received equipment to support income-generating activities under a livelihood assistance project aimed at improving economic opportunities for urban poor communities.
A total of 107 residents received sewing machines, information technology (IT) equipment and business carts at a distribution ceremony held at the Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) Auditorium on Wednesday.
The Livelihoods Support for Urban Poor Communities in Bangladesh (LSUPCB) project is implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in partnership with the Local Government Division (LGD), under the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives, with financing from the Global Development Fund (GDF) under China's South-South Cooperation.
The initiative aims to strengthen the economic resilience of vulnerable urban households through skills development, entrepreneurship support and livelihood assets, creating income opportunities for women and youth.
In DNCC, the project supports 16 low-income communities through Community Development Committees (CDCs). Beneficiaries receive 3 months of skills training, followed by productive assets based on their skills and business plans.
At the ceremony, 36 beneficiaries received sewing machines for tailoring and home-based businesses, 30 received IT equipment for digital services and technology-based enterprises, and 41 received business carts for small-scale trading.
Addressing the ceremony as the chief guest, DNCC Administrator Md Safiqul Islam Khan said: “These assets are not simply equipment; they are opportunities to build sustainable livelihoods. Beneficiaries must use them responsibly to generate income, strengthen their businesses and create a better future for their families.”
Chairing the event, DNCC Chief Executive Officer Mohammad Ashaduz Zaman said: “Skills development becomes more meaningful when people have the resources to put their training into practice. This support will help beneficiaries turn their abilities into income-generating opportunities.”
Yugesh Pradhanang, international technical adviser and project manager of the Livelihoods Improvement of Urban Poor Communities Project at UNDP Bangladesh, said: “Providing livelihood assets alongside practical training helps people move toward financial independence. Our focus is on enabling vulnerable women and youth to build sustainable livelihoods.”
The LSUPCB project operates across 6 cities and towns in Bangladesh, supporting employment, entrepreneurship and economic self-reliance among vulnerable urban communities.
Mohammad Mamun-Ul-Hassan, deputy secretary and chief social welfare and slum development officer at DNCC, delivered the welcome address.
Through government and development partnerships, the initiative seeks to strengthen household incomes, promote small-scale entrepreneurship and create sustainable economic opportunities for urban poor communities.

item.title: Hasan makes ranking leap after historic Test hat-trick
item.description:
Bangladesh fast bowler Hasan Mahmud has climbed seven places to 38th in the latest ICC Test bowlers’ rankings after his historic hat-trick against Afghanistan in the one-off Test in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.
Hasan became the first Bangladesh fast bowler to claim a hat-trick in Test cricket during Afghanistan’s first innings, when he took five wickets in total. He added another wicket in the second innings to finish with six scalps in the match.
His impressive performance helped him make significant progress in the latest rankings, while several other Bangladesh players also moved up the ladder.
Among the other Bangladesh bowlers, Ebadot Hossain made the biggest leap, climbing 11 places to 67th, while Mehidy Hasan Miraz moved up one spot to 22nd. Taijul Islam, however, dropped three places to 18th.
In the Test batters’ rankings, wicketkeeper-batter Liton Das climbed three places to joint 29th with 610 rating points after scoring 53 in the first innings and a century in the second.
Tanzid Hasan Tamim also made progress, rising 10 places to 92nd, while Nazmul Hossain Shanto and Mushfiqur Rahim each slipped one place.
Afghanistan batter Rahmat Shah climbed 13 places to 13th after scoring a century and a half-century across the two innings against Bangladesh.
Sediqullah Atal surged 41 places to 91st following a century in the fourth innings that helped Afghanistan secure a draw, while Mohammad Saleem rose 21 places to 72nd in the Test bowlers’ rankings.

item.title: Hockey team begin Asian Champions Trophy preparations
item.description:
Twenty-six provisionally selected players of the Bangladesh national hockey team reported to the training camp at Maulana Bhashani National Hockey Stadium on Wednesday ahead of the upcoming Hero Asian Champions Trophy in India.
The tournament will be held in Jalandhar and Mohali from October 27 to November 5, with Bangladesh set to compete against Asia’s leading hockey nations after being included following Pakistan’s withdrawal.
The team's first on-field training session is scheduled for Thursday under local coach Shahidullah Titu, while German coach Peter Gerhard is expected to join the camp by Friday.
Bangladesh Hockey Federation (BHF) joint secretary Ariful Haque Prince expressed optimism about the team's participation, saying the tournament would provide the players with valuable exposure to high-level international competition.
“Playing in a major event like the Asian Champions Trophy is a positive and encouraging development for Bangladesh hockey. It will give our players the opportunity to compete against Asia's top teams,” he said.
Prince added that participation in the tournament would help the team overcome the challenges posed by a prolonged absence from international competition and gain valuable experience against stronger opponents.
“Facing top teams will help our players gain valuable experience, which will contribute to improving their performance and overall standard of play. Bangladesh will compete in the tournament with the aim of strengthening its capabilities and making further progress on the international stage,” he said.
The BHF hopes the intensive training camp will help the team regain its best form and deliver a positive performance in India.
Bangladesh will join hosts India, Malaysia, Japan, South Korea and China in the six-team tournament. The Tigers are scheduled to play their opening match on October 27.

item.title: Saudi league postpones three matches after Houthi attacks
item.description:
The Saudi Arabian football league (SPL) has postponed three fixtures, including one involving Cristiano Ronaldo's Al Nassr, following the dramatic escalation in the country's war with the Houthis.
The matchweek nine fixtures have been pushed back in the calendar for "logistical considerations, taking into account the mandatory minimum rest period between matches", according to a statement published on Tuesday on the SPL's website.
The meeting between league leaders Al Hilal and Al Riyadh and the match between Al Ittihad and Al Shabab have been postponed to December 19, while the clash between Al Ahli and Ronaldo's Al Nassr has been rescheduled for March 6, 2027.
The SPL added, however, that the other matchweek nine fixtures "will be played according to the previously announced schedule with no changes".
On Monday, Al Nassr's AFC Champions League match against Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana in Riyadh was delayed by an hour after the coalition announced it had intercepted a missile fired by the Houthis towards the Saudi capital.
A violent battle between a Saudi-led coalition and Yemen's Houthis has erupted in recent days, with missile strikes on airports and energy facilities across the kingdom.
The latest round of fighting was triggered by Houthi strikes on Riyadh's international airport at the weekend that left 13 people dead and operations suspended in the worst attack since 2015.

item.title: Macron says French student protesters ‘exploited’ by political forces
item.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron believes the students waging three weeks of protests that have closed many schools have “legitimate” grievances but are also being “exploited” by political forces, a government spokeswoman said Wednesday.
The leader, who is in his final six months of office, has asked the government to come up with “concrete responses” to the unrest by high school pupils within weeks, spokeswoman Maud Bregeon told reporters.
She spoke following Macron’s weekly meeting with his cabinet, a day after nationwide solidarity demonstrations showed significant support for the students.
The interior ministry said 161,500 people turned out for Tuesday’s demonstrations held in Paris and other cities. Unions organizing the rallies put the figure at 480,000.
Some violent scenes erupted on the sidelines of marches in Paris and Lyon, with police firing tear gas in response.
In his cabinet meeting, Macron “stressed that young people have legitimate concerns, but said these are being exploited for political purposes and turned into urban violence,” Bregeon said.
With French presidential elections due in April and May next year, some opposition parties have seized upon the demonstrations.
Jean-Luc Melenchon, the presidential candidate for the far-left France Unbowed (LFI) party, participated in one of the Paris protests.
The far-right National Rally (RN) party of Marine Le Pen, whom surveys give as the frontrunner for the elections, has voiced support for police deployed to the demonstrations and blamed students for violent episodes.
Students, unions, rights groups and parents have accused the police of brutality against the students, with some of the young protesters maimed.
The family of one 15-year-old high school student who lost his hand when a police stun grenade exploded said Wednesday they had started legal action to demand an “impartial” investigation.
One of the family’s lawyers, Bertrand Wattez, said the boy, Evan, denied the police account, relayed by prosecutors, that he had tried to pick up the grenade when it went off on October 5. He also denied taking part in the student protests in his city of Lens.
The lawyer said that Evan not only lost his left hand as a result of the blast but also several fingers on his right hand.
In another violent incident, a 16-year-old student was blinded in an eye during a September 30 protest outside his school in the western city of Tours. His family blamed the police.
Late Tuesday, the prosecutor for Tours said the officer involved had been charged with aggravated battery.
Police have opened internal investigations into 36 allegations of officer violence against demonstrators, according to the interior ministry.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said Wednesday that 248 students had been injured during the protests, “most often in cases of urban violence.”
A total of 937 police officers had also been injured, as had 149 members of teaching staff, Lecornu told a parliamentary question session.
The premier alleged that the student movement had been “instrumentalized by the allies of France Unbowed... for electoral reasons.”

item.title: Govt canal grabbed by influential locals in Gopalganj
item.description:
Influential locals have allegedly occupied nearly 1km of the government-owned Loharangk Canal in Kotalipara upazila of Gopalganj, filling parts of it and building houses on the land, disrupting drainage and causing waterlogging in the area.
Although officials have identified and marked the encroached sections, the administration has yet to launch an eviction drive, prompting questions from local residents.
According to locals, several residents of Loharangk village, including Monir Biswas, Selim Biswas, Babul Molla, Imarat Molla, Amzad Molla, Mohammad Ali Daria, Sekendar Daria, Auwal Daria, Manir Daria, Kasem Daria, Ibrahim Daria, Kibria Biswas and Ratan Das, have allegedly occupied parts of the canal and built houses there.
On September 15, Farid Daria and around 100 other villagers submitted a written application to the deputy commissioner and the upazila nirbahi officer (UNO), seeking the recovery of the canal.
Following the application, officials from the district and upazila administrations visited the site, measured the canal and marked its boundaries with red flags. However, the encroached land has yet to be cleared.
Farid said some influential villagers had been occupying the canal and building houses there for around 30 years. The encroachment had left parts of the village waterlogged whenever it rained, he added.
“Officials measured the canal and marked its boundaries with red flags after receiving our application. Several days have passed, but the administration has yet to free the canal from encroachment,” he said.
Mohammad Ali Daria, one of the alleged encroachers, claimed that villagers had taken land for a public road from his property and given him part of the canal in exchange.
“If they return the land taken for the road, I will give up the canal land,” he said.
Another alleged encroacher, Monir Biswas, acknowledged building a house on the canal land, saying he would vacate it when instructed by the administration.
UNO Saif-ul-Arefeen said the authorities were still measuring the canal and determining its boundaries.
“Steps will be taken to evict the encroachers once the process is complete,” he said.

item.title: Eight members of Four Star gang held with foreign-made pistol, ammunition
item.description:
The Special Rapid Battalion (SRB) has launched a crackdown on members of the notorious “Four Star” gang operating in the capital’s Pallabi and Rupnagar areas, arresting eight of its members.
Speaking on Wednesday, SRB-4 Commander Lieutenant Colonel Hafizur Rahman said the eight were arrested during separate raids in Pallabi’s Ceramics and No12 Jhilpara areas on Tuesday night.
Seven of the arrestees are members of the Mashiur-Mamun faction of the “Four Star” gang, while another belongs to the Moktar faction.
The arrestees were identified as Jewel Rana, 26, Saimon, 20, Ramzan, 22, Bijoy, 23, Fazle Rabbi Chiku, 23, Afsar Hossain Jim, 19, Jahangir Hossain and Mission Islam alias Minhajul Islam.
SRB personnel recovered a foreign-made pistol, one round of live ammunition, yaba tablets and locally made weapons from their possession.
According to SRB, Afsar and his associate Saimon were arrested from a house in Pallabi. A foreign-made pistol and one round of live ammunition were recovered from them.
Jim is described by SRB as an emerging shooter for the Mashiur-Mamun faction. He is accused of involvement in land grabbing, confining people in hotel rooms for blackmail and extorting money from various establishments.
Saimon is also accused of supplying firearms and involvement in shooting incidents.

item.title: Durga Puja preparations going on in full swing in Tangail
item.description:
Preparations for Durga Puja are in final stages across Tangail, with artisans working day and night to complete idols and organisers putting the finishing touches to pandals ahead of the Hindu community’s biggest religious festival.
This year, 1,356 pandals will host the festival across the district’s 12 upazilas, 110 more than last year. However, artisans say soaring raw material prices and shrinking profits are making it increasingly difficult to sustain their livelihoods.
Durga Puja will begin nationwide on October 15 with Maha Panchami and conclude on October 21 with Bijoya Dashami and the immersion of idols.
Artisans are racing against time to complete idols of Goddess Durga and her children — Lakshmi, Saraswati, Kartik and Ganesha. While idol-making has been completed in many places, work continues at several others, with artisans painting idols and adding the final touches to meet deadlines.
From early morning until late at night, workers are putting in long hours as preparations gather pace and the festive atmosphere spreads across the district.
According to traditional Hindu beliefs, Goddess Durga will arrive on an elephant and depart by boat this year.
Despite the increase in the number of pandals, idol-makers say rising prices of clay, paint and other materials have significantly eroded their profits. They also say their earnings are no longer sufficient to cover household expenses.
Pradip Chandra Pal, an artisan who has been making idols for 20 years, said preparations were now at their busiest, with workers labouring day and night to finish their work.
“The cost of everything needed to make idols has increased. A colour that used to cost Tk100 now costs Tk150. The price of clay has also risen significantly,” he told Dhaka Tribune.
Pal said he had made 10 idols this year at a cost of Tk150,000 and expected to sell them for around Tk250,000.
“Earlier, we could spend six months without work after making idols for Durga Puja. Now, that is no longer possible,” he said, adding that rising costs and low returns had made the profession increasingly difficult.
Another artisan, Arnab, who has been in the profession for seven years, said the workload increased sharply ahead of the festival, leaving little time for rest.
“We hardly have any time to rest during this period. But the money we earn from painting idols is not enough to run our households,” he said.
The artisans called for government assistance to help them cope with rising production costs and declining profits.
Tangail District Puja Celebration Committee Acting President Chitta Ranjan Sarkar said organisers had held discussions with representatives of all puja committees to ensure the celebrations proceeded smoothly.
He attributed the increase in the number of pandals to the administration’s overall cooperation.
“Police will be deployed at every pandal, alongside CCTV surveillance and other security measures. We hope to complete the celebrations without any untoward incidents,” he said.
Tangail Superintendent of Police Mohammad Shamsul Alam Sarkar said a special security plan had been drawn up for the festival.
Police, Detective Branch personnel and plainclothes officers will be deployed to maintain law and order, he said, adding that the police would remain vigilant to ensure peaceful celebrations.
